commits.message:
fix(taxonomy): fix silent no-op renames, dedupe against aliases, add deterministic related titles

Bug report: "the job titles taxonomy when updated is not saving and
returning to the same state." Reproduced and root-caused: a rename that
only fixes casing/whitespace/punctuation -- "java developer" ->
"Java Developer" -- has the SAME normalized key as before, so
update_canonical_job_title's `if new_key != current_key` guard skipped
the whole rename branch and never wrote the corrected text, while still
returning {"updated": True}. The reviewer saw a "successful" save that
silently did nothing, and the row reverted to its old text on reload --
exactly the reported symptom. Same bug existed in update_canonical_skill.
Fixed in both: the corrected text is now always written whenever it
literally differs from what's stored, and the collision-check +
alias-preservation dance only runs when it's actually a different
entity (a different normalized key), not on every rename.

Also: "leave seniority as optional" -- it already was optional on the
backend (Optional[str], only applied if provided); the Job titles page
now labels the column "Seniority (optional)" so that's visible instead
of looking like a required field to fill in on every edit.

"add maximum related job titles as possible deterministically": new
compute_related_job_titles (app/understanding/taxonomy/
title_family_classifier.py) -- token-overlap matching, no LLM. Two
titles are related when they share a "core" word (a real technology/
domain term -- "java", "sap", "salesforce" -- never a bare seniority
word or a generic role suffix like "developer"/"engineer" alone, which
would match almost everything and be useless as a signal). Wired into
add_canonical_job_title (computed on every approval) and
update_canonical_job_title (recomputed whenever title or family
changes). New bulk_backfill_related_titles + POST /taxonomy/job-titles/
backfill-related-titles + a "Fill in related titles (N)" button on the
Job titles page clears the backlog of entries added before this
existed, without ever touching an entry that already has related
titles set (a reviewer may have hand-picked those).

"ensure there won't be any duplicates in skills and job title
taxonomies, and newly parsed information shouldn't show in the
blocklist and taxonomy if there are duplicates": the existing duplicate
guard on add_canonical_skill/add_canonical_job_title only compared a
new name/title against other entries' own name/title field -- a term
already recognized only as an ALIAS of something else slipped through
as if brand new (two taxonomy entries for one real skill/role,
invisible to the old check because it never looked at aliases). Fixed
to check the full alias index (canonical names + every entry's own
aliases + skill_aliases.json/title_aliases.json) instead. Same fix
applied to update_canonical_skill/update_canonical_job_title's rename
collision check.

Also added a second, stricter check for near-duplicate SPELLING (not
just exact normalized-key matches): _loose_key strips ALL punctuation
and spacing for detection purposes only (normalize_taxonomy_key
deliberately keeps '.'/'+'/'#' since those are load-bearing for real
distinct names like ".NET" vs "NET"/"C++" vs "C", which also means it
treats "Node.js" and "NodeJS" as different keys even though they're the
same skill). build_loose_skill_key_index/build_loose_title_key_index
wrap the existing alias indexes with this looser key, used to: (1)
refuse an approval whose loose key already matches an existing entry,
(2) skip queueing a newly-parsed term as an "unknown" candidate when
its loose key already matches something Hermes already recognizes, and
(3) merge a new pending candidate into an existing pending candidate
row on a loose-key match instead of creating a second near-identical
review-queue entry a human has to notice are the same thing.

New coverage in scripts/hermes-900-spam-taxonomy-check.py (15 new
checks): case-only renames actually write the corrected text (both
skills and job titles, direct regression tests for the reported bug);
related titles are found by shared core keywords and NOT by generic
role words alone (an earlier draft of compute_related_job_titles
related "Java Developer" to "Python Developer" via the word
"developer" alone -- caught and tightened before this shipped); related
titles are recomputed on update and backfilled without ever
overwriting a hand-set list; adding a skill/title already known only as
an alias, or only as a punctuation-variant spelling, is rejected as a
duplicate; a punctuation-only spelling variant of a known skill/title
is never queued as an unknown candidate. Full Python regression suite
run against a fresh schema and freshly built image: hermes-900 (the
script covering every change in this commit) passes all 69 checks
including the 15 new ones; every other failure in the suite reproduces
byte-for-byte identically against the current, unmodified production
image in the same throwaway harness (missing live server for the *-api-
check.py scripts, missing Langfuse/MS Graph credentials, missing
access-control file) -- confirmed pre-existing environment gaps, not
regressions from this change. Frontend type-checks and builds clean.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
